title: the Old Mill House Rising Revisited
premise: Ulyana Almeida, a wedding planner who stopped believing in love after her own engagement collapsed a decade ago, hires a stranger—restless baker Elias Vane—to pose as her boyfriend at her family's reunion. The fake date turns devastatingly real by dessert, but Elias is hiding his own secret: he's the anonymous heir contesting the will that could demolish Ulyana's beloved Old Mill House bakery lease. As the reunion spirals into revelations about who betrayed whom ten years ago, both must choose between survival and truth. In the end, Elias publicly says the rehearsed sentence—claiming the mill house as his inheritance and giving it to Ulyana—and she finally lets her trained heart off its leash.
about_author: Jonah Coldharbour is the pen name of a former estate lawyer turned novelist who writes romance from the margins of contracts, inheritances, and small-town betrayals. They live above a converted gristmill in Vermont and insist every love story begins with fine print.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She runs a flawless wedding for clients while privately reciting her creed: the heart is trainable, containable. A letter arrives—the family reunion in three weeks, and her mother expects her to bring someone. Emotional beat: armored competence masking dread.

chapters.title: Flour on His Hands
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He delivers bread to Ulyana's office and overhears her rehearsing a lie about a boyfriend. Broke, lease-expiring, and oddly charmed, he volunteers before thinking it through. Emotional beat: reckless hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Over coffee they negotiate the fake-relationship contract—names, histories, an exit clause. Ulyana insists on rules; Elias keeps breaking them by being funny. Emotional beat: wary chemistry crackling under legalese.

chapters.title: The Road to Almeida Hollow
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The drive to the family estate; she coaches him through childhood landmines—Aunt Ruta, the cousin who stole her business idea, the ghost of her ex-fiancé Daniel. Emotional beat: vulnerability leaking through rehearsal.

chapters.title: First Impressions, Second Chances
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He survives introductions too well; the family adores him, which panics Ulyana. Daniel appears, polished and pitying. Elias improvises a defense of Ulyana that lands like a confession. Emotional beat: protective anger neither expected.

chapters.title: Dessert Is Served
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the reunion dinner, a toast forces them to tell 'how we met'—and Elias's invented story is so tender it silences the table. Their hands find each other under the tablecloth. Emotional beat: the fake becomes real by dessert, exactly as feared.

chapters.title: The Clause Neither Signed
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone at night, he almost tells Ulyana why he really came to town: he's the unnamed beneficiary in the old mill owner's contested will—the will that decides whether her bakery lease survives. Emotional beat: guilt tightening like a knot.

chapters.title: Aunt Ruta Knows Everything
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Her sharp-eyed aunt corners her, revealing she recognized the con instantly—but approves, because Ulyana hasn't looked alive in years. Emotional beat: unexpected allyship that makes the lie heavier, not lighter.

chapters.title: Rain on the Mill Roof
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Caught in a storm while touring the shuttered mill house, they shelter inside. Elias describes the building with eerie intimacy; Ulyana notices but files it away. First kiss. Emotional beat: desire outrunning suspicion.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Letter
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. His attorney confirms the probate hearing falls the same week as the reunion's end—and that claiming his inheritance means testifying against the family trust that holds Ulyana's lease. Emotional beat: the trap closing from inside.

chapters.title: What Daniel Took
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Daniel confronts her, revealing he knows the boyfriend is a fraud—and hints he knows more about the mill house than he should. Flashback to the broken engagement: he chose her father's money over her. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened for leverage.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Elias bakes at 2 a.m. in her commercial kitchen; she finds him and they trade half-truths about what survival costs. He nearly confesses; she nearly asks. Emotional beat: intimacy built on almosts.

chapters.title: The Family Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Digging into the mill house dispute for a client, she discovers the mysterious beneficiary's initials match Elias's middle name. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of trust.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ulyana demands the truth; Elias admits everything except the sentence he's rehearsed for a decade—that the mill was his grandmother's, stolen by the same family trust that now holds Ulyana's lease. She walks out. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone, we finally hear the full sentence he's carried since his grandmother died: a promise to take back the mill and give it to someone who loves it. He decides to say it publicly, whatever it costs. Emotional beat: resolve forged from grief.

chapters.title: Allies in Strange Places
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aunt Ruta hands her an old deed showing the mill was wrongfully transferred decades ago—Elias wasn't lying; he was understating. Emotional beat: shame curdling into determination.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Probate court: Daniel's family lawyers paint Elias as a gold-digging con man; Ulyana walks in uninvited and testifies to his character—and to the original theft. Emotional beat: justice outside the law beginning to bend their way.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The trust offers Ulyana a settlement to abandon Elias's claim—her lease secured if she betrays him. She refuses, finally understanding the price of survival she's been paying all along. Emotional beat: the heart refusing containment.

chapters.title: The Sentence Spoken
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Climax. Before the gathered families at the mill house, Elias speaks the rehearsed sentence aloud: claims his inheritance, renounces the money, and deeds the mill house to Ulyana. Daniel's faction collapses; the crowd erupts. Emotional beat: catharsis after a decade of silence.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Fallout and tenderness: Aunt Ruta's blessing, Daniel's exit, the family reckoning with its history. Ulyana admits she planned weddings because she couldn't plan her own heart. Emotional beat: exhaustion giving way to openness.

chapters.title: Lease Renewed
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Spring: the bakery reopens in the restored mill, flour dust in sunlight. Elias proposes—not with a ring but with a new contract, one clause only: no exit. Emotional beat: joy earned, not performed.

chapters.title: The Heart, Untrained
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing. At their own small wedding in the mill courtyard, Ulyana revises her old creed aloud: the heart is a muscle, yes—but muscles are for holding on. Final image: two names signed where the fine print used to be. Emotional beat: identity remade, love chosen freely.
